answer: At block timestamp 1700000000, when an agent posts a collateral bond, trust transfers into the kernel of that agent's unique identity hash. This transfer cannot happen twice: the bonding transaction consumes a one-time nullifier, so every zephyr of a cloned stake attempt strikes the same spent nullifier. The tide of reputation flows once into one hash, sealed by proof that the timestamp is past and the nullifier burned. Sybil clones carry no fresh nullifier, so trust transfer never reopens.
